data.content_ref: inline:The target identifies latent heat / evapotranspiration as the single mechanism explaining cross-city variation, claiming arid cities have a LARGER nocturnal UHI because the urban-rural latent heat contrast is maximized, while humid cities have a smaller gap. But in arid regions the surrounding countryside has little moisture and therefore little evapotranspirative cooling, so the rural side also cannot cool as effectively at night — reducing, not maximizing, the urban-rural temperature gap. Empirically, nocturnal UHI is often most pronounced in humid climates with dense vegetation contrast (e.g., Atlanta vs. humid Southeastern countryside), because the rural countryside cools efficiently via evapotranspiration while impervious city surfaces cannot. The directionality asserted in the mechanism is therefore backwards.
